title: Changing Freezer Multisig signers requires an Atlas Edit Proposal, and unexplained changes are presumed malicious
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.3.5 states that "Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal," with exactly two exceptions: a signer self-reporting "a loss of access to their private key," or a signer expressing "their wish to be removed." Both exceptions require "a public Sky Forum post."

The enforcement clause is what gives this force: "Any changes to the Multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, **should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious**. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the Multisig."

This is a rare instance of a governance document specifying a default interpretation of an anomaly. Rather than requiring proof of bad intent, it makes an unexplained roster change *presumptively* an attack and assigns a named actor a mandatory response. Detection does not depend on someone deciding whether to be suspicious.

The contrast with the Relayer multisigs is the whole point. Obex "can change the signers of the Prime Relayer Multisig **at any time**, so long as there are at least seven (7) signers and at least a majority of signers are required" (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5), and Soter Labs has an equivalent freedom over its own. Operating keys are self-managed under structural constraints; the keys that can halt the system are locked at ecosystem level, because the ability to quietly replace the watchdog is worth more to an attacker than the ability to replace an operator.
description: Only a self-reported key loss or a voluntary resignation, each announced on the Forum, bypasses Sky Governance; anything else triggers an expedited Executive Vote to strip the multisig's access.
